references.name: Adam Smith
references.connection:
Source of the barter myth; Graeber systematically
demolishes his foundational historical claim.

references.name: Marcel Mauss
references.connection:
First to recognize the complexity of non-commercial exchange;
Graeber's acknowledged intellectual ancestor.

references.name: Orlando Patterson
references.connection:
Foundational definition of slavery as natal alienation;
central to Ch. 7 analysis of honor and degradation.

references.name: Caroline Humphrey
references.connection:
Definitive anthropological refutation of barter-origin
stories: "No example of a barter economy has ever been found."

references.name: Alfred Mitchell-Innes
references.connection:
Credit theory of money: "Our standard account of monetary
history is precisely backwards."

references.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
references.connection:
Argued morality descended from creditor-debtor relations;
Graeber agrees with the observation but refutes the premise.

references.name: Karl Jaspers
references.connection:
Graeber expands Jaspers' framework and adds the
coinage-philosophy connection Jaspers missed.

references.name: Al-Ghazali
references.connection:
Islamic economist whose money-as-mirror theory and
pin-factory illustration Adam Smith borrowed without credit.

references.name: Michael Hudson
references.connection:
First to identify U.S. Treasury bonds as permanent tribute
rather than genuine financial obligations.

references.name: Fernand Braudel
references.connection:
Markets-vs.-capitalism distinction;
China as anti-capitalist market state.

references.name: G.F. Knapp
references.connection:
Chartalism: money is whatever the state accepts in taxes;
taxes create markets.

references.name: Richard Seaford
references.desc: Money and the Early Greek Mind
references.connection:
Coins as philosophically novel objects — material and
abstract simultaneously — explaining the origins of Platonic dualism.

references.name: Moses Finley
references.connection:
"In the ancient world, all revolutionary movements had
a single program: cancel the debts and redistribute the land."

references.name: George Gilder
references.connection:
Supply-side theology: investors create value ex nihilo like God;
the creditor's religion of the Reagan revolution.

references.name: Craig Muldrew
